\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:exp}

% Tables are generated by scripts/paper_artifacts.py into docs/tables/ and are
% pulled in below at the point each is discussed. Do not edit them by hand: the
% generator reads the tuned thresholds from the file the tuning run wrote, which
% is what stops the prose and the tables from drifting apart.

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:protocol}

\paragraph{Data.} We evaluate on a Replica-derived benchmark with $17$ scenes
split $11/3/3$ into train, validation and test, and two independent pose
collections, $\texttt{f}$ and $\texttt{g}$, over the same rooms. Each pose has a
$640{\times}480$ image and a room impulse response from a six-microphone ring of
radius $5$\,cm with a co-located source, rendered at $48$\,kHz with reflection
depth $50$ and diffraction to order $10$. Two acoustic conditions exist per pose:
\texttt{raw\_scan\_open} on the full furnished mesh, and
\texttt{floorplan\_closed} on walls alone.

\textbf{Queries are always \texttt{raw\_scan\_open}; candidates are always
\texttt{floorplan\_closed}.} A deployment has a floorplan and cannot render
furniture it does not know about, so any result that uses a furnished candidate
grid is reported only as an upper bound (Sec.~\ref{sec:bounds}).

\paragraph{Protocol.} Every design choice, including the acoustic feature, the
fusion structure and the four scalars, is selected on \texttt{replica\_f}. Every
number we report is measured on the disjoint \texttt{replica\_g}, $300$ queries.
Gains carry $95\%$ paired bootstrap intervals over queries, because the two
predictions for a query are not independent and an unpaired interval would be
far too wide. We state plainly that this holds out the pose collection rather
than the room; see Sec.~\ref{sec:limits}.

\paragraph{Metrics.} We report recall at $0.1$, $0.5$, $1$, $2$ and $5$\,m, the
joint $1$\,m\,/\,$30^\circ$ recall, median error and RMSE, using the error
definitions of \cite{f3loc} and the thresholds of \cite{unloc}.

\paragraph{Backbones.} We attach the acoustic term to two single-image
floorplan localisers, F3Loc \cite{f3loc} (monocular) and UnLoc \cite{unloc},
both trained on the Replica training split. Neither is modified.

\input{tables/tab_repro}

\subsection{Baselines are correctly reproduced}
\label{sec:repro}

Since our contribution is measured as a delta on top of existing methods, a
mis-reproduced baseline would invalidate every number. Tab.~\ref{tab:repro}
reproduces the published tables of three prior methods from released weights
under the authors' own protocols. F3Loc's three rows and UnLoc's seven
thresholds match to within $0.1$ point; DisCo-FLoc matches to within $1.0$.

One detail is worth recording because it silently changes conclusions. F3Loc's
evaluation leaves its monocular and multi-view networks in training mode, so
BatchNorm uses batch statistics and the score depends on the evaluation batch
size: the monocular network reads $46.8\%$ at batch $16$ and $36.5\%$ at
batch $1$. All our evaluations force batch $1$ and record the batch size in
every metrics file.

\subsection{Main results}
\label{sec:main}

\input{tables/tab_main}
\input{tables/tab_scenes}

Tab.~\ref{tab:main} is the headline. Adding the acoustic term, with the visual
weights untouched, improves recall at $1$\,m by $8.0$ points
$[3.3, 12.7]$ on F3Loc and $5.0$ points $[0.7, 9.3]$ on UnLoc. Median error
roughly halves on both, $2.17 \to 1.20$\,m and $1.12 \to 0.51$\,m, and RMSE over
all queries falls, so the improvement is a reduction in large failures rather
than a sharpening of successes.

The gain is confined to a band. At $0.5$, $1$ and $2$\,m it is between $5$ and
$10$ points; at $0.1$\,m it is within noise, and at $5$\,m the backbones are
already near saturation. This follows from the formulation: selecting among
hypotheses cannot refine a position within a hypothesis, and $0.1$\,m is one
grid cell. We regard stating this as more useful than reporting only the
thresholds that flatter the method.

Tab.~\ref{tab:scenes} breaks the result down by room. The two backbones improve
in different rooms, and in each case the improvement is largest where that
backbone is weakest: F3Loc gains $14$ points in the room where it reaches
$15\%$ and loses $3$ where it reaches $76\%$; UnLoc gains $15$ where it reaches
$24\%$. Sound is not better in some rooms than others. It is useful wherever the
visual posterior is failing, which is a property of the pair, not the room.

\subsection{Ablations}
\label{sec:ablation}

\input{tables/tab_fusion}
\input{tables/tab_feature}

\paragraph{Fusion rule.} Tab.~\ref{tab:fusion} varies only the combination rule.
Three rows matter. Unconditional reranking among hypotheses loses $15.7$ points:
sound cannot be trusted to choose by itself. Both cell-wise rules have intervals
that span zero, so on this data they are not established gains. Replacing the
smooth gate \eqref{eq:gamma} by a hard threshold costs $9.3$ points and turns
the result negative, because near either boundary a hard rule commits fully on
an arbitrarily small difference.

\paragraph{Acoustic feature.} Tab.~\ref{tab:feature} shows the criterion
disagreement of Sec.~\ref{sec:acoustic} directly. Ordered by how well sound
localises alone, the $2$\,ms envelope is best at $22.3\%$ and our spectrogram is
second. Ordered by how often the feature picks the correct hypothesis, our
spectrogram leads by $6.0$ points and the envelope is fifth. Selecting on
\texttt{replica\_f} alone yields the same winner as selecting on the pooled
data, so the choice is not a test-set artefact.

\paragraph{Prior claim revisited.} Banded spectrograms were previously rejected
for this task as smearing each frame over $8$\,ms. That was measured at
$8$\,kHz, where $n_{\mathrm{fft}}{=}64$ spans $8$\,ms. At the $48$\,kHz of the
current data the same window spans $1.33$\,ms, and our sweep finds the best
setting at $5.33$\,ms. Frequency resolution, not time resolution, governs
discrimination between hypotheses.

\subsection{When does sound help, and does it know?}
\label{sec:analysis}

\paragraph{The gain lives in visual ambiguity.} Binning queries by the log-odds
between the two strongest hypotheses, the net gain is $+12.5$ points in the most
ambiguous fifth, decreasing monotonically to $-15.0$ in the least ambiguous
fifth. This is the behaviour \eqref{eq:gamma} is designed to exploit and it
validates gating on $m_v$.

\paragraph{Sound does not know when it is wrong.} We tested every acoustic
self-confidence measure available at inference as a predictor of three events:
whether the acoustic pick is correct, whether it repairs the visual prediction,
and whether it breaks it. None exceeds $\mathrm{AUROC}\ 0.60$. The best
predictor of an acoustic \emph{mistake} is the visual quantity $m_v$, at
$0.626$. Comparing the $300$ queries the acoustic term repairs against those it
breaks, the central $90\%$ of the latter distribution contains $98\%$ of the
former under \eqref{eq:evidence}: the two are the same event with a different
answer.

We therefore report the second gate as an ablation, not a contribution. On one
backbone its tuned threshold is $-\infty$, i.e.\ it switches itself off, and
\eqref{eq:gamma} collapses to a gate on visual ambiguity. Building a reliable
acoustic self-confidence signal remains open.

\paragraph{Late reflections do not carry the information the story predicts.}
A natural motivation for acoustic assistance is that late arrivals have visited
regions the camera cannot see. Splitting the post-direct response into ranges
contradicts it: the $64$--$128$\,ms range alone places the true pose at the
$39.8$th percentile, \emph{below chance}, and every late-only range is worse
than every early one. Cumulative windows still improve monotonically because
the early part dominates. Under this domain gap, late energy is furniture
mismatch, not non-line-of-sight geometry.

\subsection{What limits the method}
\label{sec:bounds}

\input{tables/tab_bounds}

Tab.~\ref{tab:bounds} bounds the problem from two sides.

An oracle that selects the best of the ten hypotheses reaches $93.7\%$ against
our $54.7\%$. Roughly $39$ points remain available to a better acoustic
discriminator without changing anything else, so the shortlist is not the
binding constraint.

Replacing the furnished query with one rendered on the same wall-only mesh as
the candidates, changing nothing else, moves the acoustic score from $20.7\%$ to
$94.3\%$ alone and the median ground-truth rank from $192$ to $1$. The furniture
domain gap, not the fusion, is what limits the method.

That control also inverts the ordering of the rules. With matched geometry,
unconditional reranking is the best rule and every gate costs points, including
ours, which reaches $65.7\%$ where the ungated acoustic score reaches $94.3\%$.
Our gating machinery is compensating for the domain gap, and would be actively
harmful if the gap were closed.

We attempted to close it without using furniture. A per-component reliability
weight, estimated from paired furnished and wall-only recordings on the eleven
training rooms, correlates $0.04$ and $-0.05$ with the same quantity measured in
two of the three test rooms: it is a per-room fit. A small paired regression from
the furnished to the wall-only domain, trained on the same rooms with exact
supervision, improves the held-out regression loss threefold, $1.253 \to 0.391$,
and leaves the median ground-truth rank unchanged, $297$ against $298$. It
learned the average effect of furniture, which is common to every candidate and
therefore cancels in a ranking. Both are reported as negative results.

\subsection{Limitations}
\label{sec:limits}

\textbf{Both acoustic domains are simulated.} The furnished and wall-only
conditions differ only in mesh and come from the same engine. Nothing here
establishes that a real microphone in a real room behaves this way, and we
regard validation on measured impulse responses as the necessary next step.

\textbf{Three test rooms and $300$ held-out queries.} The held-out split
separates pose collections, not rooms; whether the four scalars transfer to an
unseen room is untested.

\textbf{A candidate grid must be pre-rendered per floorplan}, thousands of cells
per scene. This is an offline cost, but a real one.

\textbf{The gain does not extend to fine localisation.} At $0.1$\,m the method
is within noise of the backbone by construction.

\textbf{Sound supplies no heading.} The acoustic score is one number per cell,
flat across the $36$ yaw bins, so every reported orientation is the backbone's
own at the selected cell.
